1 · Bring your cards in

Drop your Deck Tradr export here A .csv file. Or click to choose one.
Or paste the text instead

Open the file, select all, copy, then paste it here. Useful when the file picker will not show your export.

It reads any spreadsheet with a name column. Price, market, cost and quantity columns are picked up automatically when they exist, whatever they happen to be called. Dropping a second file only adds what is new, so nothing gets doubled. Tick the box above only when you really do want another copy of everything.

2 · Fill in the prices

Looks up every card with no price yet and fills in its market value. Needs internet, so do this at home, not at the show.

Each picture is shrunk before it is saved, so all of them together take a few megabytes rather than twenty five. Once fetched they show with no signal.

Prices come from TCGdex, which carries TCGplayer market values and refreshes daily. No account or key is needed. Cards are matched on their set and number rather than their name, because dozens of cards share a name and only one has your number. Sealed boxes are not carried by any card service, so type those prices yourself. Sold prices are not available anywhere either, so check your best cards by eye.

3 · Condition

Your export already records what shape each card is in, and until now the app quoted every one of them at the near mint price. No price service will sell a played figure a browser can fetch for free, so this takes a percentage off per grade, the way the rest of the trade does.

These start at the overlap of two published guides, which disagreed by up to fifteen points. Treat them as a starting point you argue from. Good cards hold their value better than these numbers suggest and commons hold it worse, so lean softer on your best cards.

4 · Check it over

Tap any card to fix its price, name or condition. A scan can name a card confidently and still pick the wrong version, and the price comes along with it.

This device is running checking\u2026. The number comes from what is actually stored on the device, not from what the page claims, so it cannot tell you it updated when it did not.

Every value here is what the tracker said on 24 August 2026, the day the lot was bought. It never changes, so the profit on a card you sell in November is still measured against what you actually paid for it. The twelve marked Not in Deck Tradr were in the binder that day and are not in your export now, so they are set to sold already. Type what you got for them.
